title: Newcastle close in on £3m signing of Switzerland defender Fabian Schär
trail: Newcastle United are close to completing the £3m signing of the Switzerland central defender Fabian Schar from Deportivo La Coruña
body: Newcastle United are close to completing the £3m signing of the Switzerland central defender Fabian Schär from Deportivo La Coruña. Providing Schär passes the medical he underwent on Wednesday on Tyneside, the 26-year-old will become the fourth recruit of a frustrating summer transfer window in which Rafael Benítez appears increasingly unhappy at having to operate within the confines of a sell-to-buy policy. Newcastle’s manager has entered the final year of his St James’ Park contract and is refusing to sign an extension until Mike Ashley, the club’s owner, offers him assurances over transfer budget and plans to overhaul the academy and Under-23 side. As yet there is no sign of these guarantees materialising but, thanks to a release clause in Schär’s contract triggered by Deportivo’s relegation from La Liga, he is available for £3m. A ball-playing defender with a reputation as a dead-ball specialist, Schär has won 42 caps for Switzerland and started all three group games at the recent World Cup finals in Russia. The former Basel and Hoffenheim defender now seems set to follow the former Sparta Prague goalkeeper Martin Dubravka, the former Swansea midfielder Ki Sung-yueng and Chelsea loanee Kenedy in moving to Tyneside this summer. With Florian Lejeune having sustained a potentially serious knee injury in the past week, Schar’s imminent arrival is welcome. And particularly after Tuesday night’s underwhelming 2-2 friendly draw at Hull City where Benítez stated that his existing playing staff is not strong enough. “Is the current squad good enough for what we need?” he said, somewhat pointedly. “I don’t think so. It needs additions, that is clear. It is clear what we have to do.” Benítez hopes to be allowed to trigger the £16.5m release clause in the West Brom forward Salomón Rondón’s contract, but first he must sell Alekdsandar Mitrovic and Fulham are stalling on meeting Newcastle’s £20m asking price for the Serbia centre forward. A loan swap deal involving Rondón and Newcastle’s Dwight Gayle has been mooted while Benítez is also pursuing the possibility of acquiring the 26-year-old Japan forward Yoshinori Muto from Mainz for around £9m. So far this summer, Benítez has offloaded the midfielder Mikel Merino to Real Sociedad for £10m, the defender Chancel Mbemba to Porto for £8m and the midfielder Jack Colback to Nottingham Forest on a season-long loan. He is also close to moving the unwanted goalkeeper Matz Sells to Strasbourg before his squad’s forthcoming tour of Portugal.
